title: "Project 2026"
output: html_document
date: "2026-11-19"

```{r setup}

###############################################################################
# GSE80655 (Ramaker et al. 2017, Genome Medicine)
# PART 1 — Explore, preprocess and quality-control the data
###############################################################################

## ---- 0. Packages ------------------------------------------------------------
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "pheatmap", "patchwork"))
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "edgeR", "limma", "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75"))

library(tidyverse)
library(DESeq2)
library(edgeR)
library(limma)
library(pheatmap)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(2026)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)


## ---- 1. Read the data -------------------------------------------------------
counts_raw <- read.csv("/Users/kathykorasak/Data/GSE80655_counts.csv",   check.names = FALSE)
meta_raw   <- read.csv("/Users/kathykorasak/Data/GSE80655_metadata.csv", check.names = FALSE,
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Counts: first column = gene IDs, keep only numeric (sample) columns
gene_ids <- as.character(counts_raw[[1]])
is_num   <- vapply(counts_raw, is.numeric, logical(1))
counts   <- as.matrix(counts_raw[, is_num, drop = FALSE])
rownames(counts) <- make.unique(sub("\\..*$", "", gene_ids))  # drop ENSG version suffix

# If genes ended up as columns, transpose (genes should be rows)
if (nrow(counts) < ncol(counts)) counts <- t(counts)

###############################################################################
# Q1. How many samples and features? What type is each variable?
###############################################################################
dim(counts)                       # paper: 57,905 genes x 281 samples
dim(meta_raw)
str(meta_raw)
head(counts[, 1:5])

# Are counts raw integers? (needed for DESeq2)
all(counts == round(counts))
range(counts)

# Find the metadata column whose values match the count-matrix column names
id_col <- names(meta_raw)[vapply(meta_raw,
            function(x) mean(colnames(counts) %in% as.character(x)) > 0.9,
            logical(1))][1]
id_col

# ---- EDIT the right-hand sides to match names(meta_raw) --------------------
names(meta_raw)

col_map <- c(sample    = id_col,
             region    = "brain_region",        # AnCg / DLPFC / nAcc
             diagnosis = "diagnosis",           # Control / Major Depression / Bipolar Disorder / Schizophrenia
             age       = "age",
             sex       = "sex",
             ph        = "brain_pH",
             pmi       = "PMI",
             race      = "ethnicity",
             donor     = "donor_id")            # subject ID (if present)

meta <- meta_raw %>% select(any_of(col_map))    # renames + drops missing ones

# If there is no donor column, derive it from the sample title, e.g.
# meta$donor <- sub("_(AnCg|DLPFC|nAcc).*$", "", meta_raw$title)

# Recode empty strings / text placeholders as real NAs
meta <- meta %>% mutate(across(where(is.character),
          ~ na_if(na_if(na_if(trimws(.x), ""), "NA"), "unknown")))

# Variable types
meta <- meta %>% mutate(
  region    = factor(region),
  diagnosis = factor(diagnosis),
  sex       = factor(sex),
  across(any_of(c("race", "donor")), factor),
  across(any_of(c("age", "ph", "pmi")), as.numeric))

meta$diagnosis <- relevel(meta$diagnosis,
                          ref = grep("ctl|control", levels(meta$diagnosis),
                                     ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1])

# Align metadata rows with count columns
meta   <- meta[match(colnames(counts), meta$sample), ]
stopifnot(identical(meta$sample, colnames(counts)))
rownames(meta) <- meta$sample

# Overview tables
summary(meta)
table(meta$region, meta$diagnosis)
table(meta$diagnosis, meta$sex)

if ("donor" %in% names(meta)) {
  n_distinct(meta$donor)                 # paper: 96 donors
  table(table(meta$donor))               # how many regions per donor
}


###############################################################################
# Q2. Missing values: where, why, and how to handle
###############################################################################
sum(is.na(counts))                       # expect 0
colSums(is.na(meta))

# Visual map of missingness in the metadata
meta %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), is.na)) %>%
  rowid_to_column("row") %>%
  pivot_longer(-row, names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing") %>%
  ggplot(aes(variable, row, fill = missing)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey85", `TRUE` = "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Missing values in metadata", y = "sample") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
ggsave("figures/Q2_missingness.png", width = 7, height = 5)

# Is missingness related to diagnosis or region? (MCAR check)
for (v in c("age", "ph", "pmi")) if (v %in% names(meta) && any(is.na(meta[[v]]))) {
  print(v); print(table(missing = is.na(meta[[v]]), meta$diagnosis))
  print(fisher.test(table(is.na(meta[[v]]), meta$diagnosis), simulate.p.value = TRUE))
}

# "Structural" missingness: donors missing one or more brain regions
if ("donor" %in% names(meta)) {
  meta %>%
    dplyr::count(donor, region) %>%
    tidyr::complete(donor, region, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(n == 0) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::distinct(meta, donor, diagnosis),
      by = "donor"
    )
}
# Handling: impute numeric covariates with the overall median (NOT per diagnosis,
# which would leak the outcome), and keep a flag so the choice is transparent.
for (v in c("age", "ph", "pmi")) if (v %in% names(meta) && any(is.na(meta[[v]]))) {
  meta[[paste0(v, "_imputed")]] <- is.na(meta[[v]])
  meta[[v]][is.na(meta[[v]])]   <- median(meta[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

###############################################################################
# Q3. Samples or features that behave unlike the rest
###############################################################################
## 3a. Sample-level QC metrics
qc <- tibble(sample      = colnames(counts),
             lib_size    = colSums(counts),
             n_detected  = colSums(counts > 0),
             pct_top100  = apply(counts, 2, function(x)
                             sum(sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)[1:100]) / sum(x) * 100)) %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")

summary(qc$lib_size)

p1 <- ggplot(qc, aes(region, lib_size / 1e6, colour = diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + geom_jitter(width = .2, size = 1) +
  labs(y = "Library size (millions)")
p2 <- ggplot(qc, aes(region, n_detected, colour = diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + geom_jitter(width = .2, size = 1) +
  labs(y = "Genes with count > 0")
p1 / p2
ggsave("figures/Q3_sample_qc.png", width = 8, height = 7)

# Flag samples > 3 MAD from the median on log library size / detected genes
mad_out <- function(x) abs(x - median(x)) > 3 * mad(x)
qc <- qc %>% mutate(flag_libsize  = mad_out(log10(lib_size)),
                    flag_detected = mad_out(n_detected))
qc %>% filter(flag_libsize | flag_detected)

# Is library size associated with diagnosis? (technical vs biology)
kruskal.test(lib_size ~ diagnosis, data = qc)

## 3b. Sex check — XIST (female) vs RPS4Y1 (male) before X/Y genes are removed
sex_genes <- c(XIST = "ENSG00000229807", RPS4Y1 = "ENSG00000129824")
if (all(sex_genes %in% rownames(counts))) {
  cpm_all <- cpm(counts, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1)
  sexdf <- tibble(sample = colnames(counts),
                  XIST   = cpm_all[sex_genes["XIST"], ],
                  RPS4Y1 = cpm_all[sex_genes["RPS4Y1"], ]) %>% left_join(meta, by = "sample")
  ggplot(sexdf, aes(XIST, RPS4Y1, colour = sex)) + geom_point() +
    labs(title = "Sex check: recorded sex vs sex-chromosome expression")
  ggsave("figures/Q3_sex_check.png", width = 6, height = 5)
}

## 3c. Sample–sample correlation (on a quick log-CPM)
logcpm_raw <- cpm(counts, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1)
keep_tmp   <- rowMeans(logcpm_raw) > 1
cor_mat    <- cor(logcpm_raw[keep_tmp, ], method = "spearman")
qc$median_cor <- apply(cor_mat, 1, function(r) median(r[-which.max(r)]))
ann <- data.frame(region = meta$region, diagnosis = meta$diagnosis, row.names = meta$sample)
pheatmap(cor_mat, annotation_col = ann, show_rownames = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE,
         main = "Sample-sample Spearman correlation",
         filename = "figures/Q3_cor_heatmap.png", width = 9, height = 8)
qc %>% arrange(median_cor) %>% select(sample, region, diagnosis, median_cor) %>% head(10)

## 3d. Feature-level behaviour
gene_stats <- tibble(gene      = rownames(counts),
                     total     = rowSums(counts),
                     pct_zero  = rowMeans(counts == 0) * 100)
sum(gene_stats$total == 0)                      # genes never detected
ggplot(gene_stats, aes(log10(total + 1))) + geom_histogram(bins = 80) +
  labs(title = "Total counts per gene", x = "log10(total count + 1)")
ggsave("figures/Q3_gene_totals.png", width = 6, height = 4)
gene_stats %>% arrange(desc(total)) %>% head(20)  # dominating genes (MT-, rRNA?)

###############################################################################
# Q4. Pre-processing: annotation, filtering, normalization, transformation
###############################################################################
## 4a. Remove X/Y-chromosome genes (as in the paper; sex is ~5:1 male)
if (requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75", quietly = TRUE)) {   # = GRCh37 E75, as in paper
  gi  <- ensembldb::genes(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75::EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75)
  chr <- as.character(GenomicRanges::seqnames(gi))[match(rownames(counts), gi$gene_id)]
  table(chr %in% c("X", "Y"))
  counts_auto <- counts[!(chr %in% c("X", "Y")), ]
} else counts_auto <- counts

## 4b. Remove outlier samples decided in Q3 (EDIT this vector and justify it)
drop_samples <- character(0)   # e.g. c("GSM2xxxxxx")
counts_qc <- counts_auto[, !colnames(counts_auto) %in% drop_samples]
meta_qc   <- droplevels(meta[colnames(counts_qc), ])

## 4c. Filter lowly expressed genes (edgeR::filterByExpr, grouped by region x diagnosis)
grp  <- interaction(meta_qc$region, meta_qc$diagnosis)
keep <- filterByExpr(counts_qc, group = grp, min.count = 10)
table(keep)
counts_f <- counts_qc[keep, ]

# Before/after density plot of log-CPM
dens <- function(m, lab) as_tibble(cpm(m, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1)[, 1:30]) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>% mutate(step = lab)
bind_rows(dens(counts_qc, "before filtering"), dens(counts_f, "after filtering")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, group = name)) + geom_density(alpha = .3) + facet_wrap(~step) +
  labs(x = "log2 CPM", title = "Effect of low-count filtering (30 samples shown)")
ggsave("figures/Q4_filtering.png", width = 9, height = 4)

## 4d. Normalization (DESeq2 median-of-ratios) + variance-stabilizing transform
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = round(counts_f), colData = meta_qc,
                              design = ~ region + diagnosis)
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)
summary(sizeFactors(dds))
plot(sizeFactors(dds), colSums(counts_f) / 1e6,
     xlab = "DESeq2 size factor", ylab = "Library size (M)")

vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)          # blind = TRUE: unbiased by design for QC
vmat <- assay(vsd)

# Mean-variance before/after transformation
raw_norm <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)
mv <- bind_rows(
  tibble(mean = rowMeans(log2(raw_norm + 1)), sd = rowSds(log2(raw_norm + 1)), data = "log2(norm + 1)"),
  tibble(mean = rowMeans(vmat), sd = rowSds(vmat), data = "VST"))
ggplot(mv, aes(rank(mean), sd)) + geom_point(alpha = .05, size = .3) +
  geom_smooth(colour = "red") + facet_wrap(~data) + labs(x = "rank(mean)")
ggsave("figures/Q4_mean_sd.png", width = 9, height = 4)

# Boxplots of samples: raw vs normalized + transformed
bind_rows(
  as_tibble(log2(counts_f[, 1:40] + 1)) %>% pivot_longer(everything()) %>% mutate(step = "log2 raw"),
  as_tibble(vmat[, 1:40]) %>% pivot_longer(everything()) %>% mutate(step = "VST normalized")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(name, value)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + facet_wrap(~step, ncol = 1) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) + labs(x = "sample (first 40)")
ggsave("figures/Q4_boxplots.png", width = 9, height = 6)

###############################################################################
# Q5. Do samples cluster by biology or by a technical factor?
###############################################################################
run_pca <- function(mat, md, ntop = 500) {
  sel <- head(order(rowVars(mat), decreasing = TRUE), ntop)
  pc  <- prcomp(t(mat[sel, ]))
  list(pc = pc, var = round(100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2), 1),
       df = bind_cols(md, as_tibble(pc$x[, 1:10])))
}

## 5a. All samples
pca_all <- run_pca(vmat, meta_qc %>% left_join(select(qc, sample, lib_size, n_detected), by = "sample"))
pa <- ggplot(pca_all$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = region)) + geom_point() +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_all$var[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_all$var[2], "%)"))
pb <- ggplot(pca_all$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = diagnosis)) + geom_point()
pc_ <- ggplot(pca_all$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = log10(lib_size))) + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c()
pd <- ggplot(pca_all$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = sex)) + geom_point()
(pa | pb) / (pc_ | pd)
ggsave("figures/Q5_pca_all.png", width = 11, height = 8)

## 5b. Association of top PCs with every covariate (biological + technical)
covs <- intersect(c("region", "diagnosis", "sex", "race", "age", "ph", "pmi",
                    "lib_size", "n_detected"), names(pca_all$df))
assoc <- expand_grid(PC = paste0("PC", 1:10), cov = covs) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(p = {
    x <- pca_all$df[[cov]]; y <- pca_all$df[[PC]]
    if (is.numeric(x)) cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value
    else kruskal.test(y ~ factor(x))$p.value
  }) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(PC = factor(PC, paste0("PC", 1:10)))
ggplot(assoc, aes(PC, cov, fill = -log10(p))) + geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", "")), size = 5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + labs(title = "PC-covariate association (* p < 0.05)", y = NULL)
ggsave("figures/Q5_pc_covariate_assoc.png", width = 8, height = 4.5)

## 5c. Within each region (region dominates, so look inside it)
plots <- lapply(levels(meta_qc$region), function(r) {
  idx <- meta_qc$region == r
  p   <- run_pca(vmat[, idx], meta_qc[idx, ])
  ggplot(p$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = diagnosis)) + geom_point() +
    stat_ellipse(level = .68) +
    labs(title = r, x = paste0("PC1 (", p$var[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", p$var[2], "%)"))
})
wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 3)
ggsave("figures/Q5_pca_by_region.png", width = 14, height = 4.5)

## 5d. Hierarchical clustering (Ward, Euclidean — as in the paper)
sel <- head(order(rowVars(vmat), decreasing = TRUE), 1000)
hc  <- hclust(dist(t(vmat[sel, ])), method = "ward.D2")
pheatmap(vmat[sel, ], scale = "row", cluster_cols = hc, annotation_col = ann[colnames(vmat), ],
         show_rownames = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE,
         main = "Top 1000 variable genes (row z-scores)",
         filename = "figures/Q5_heatmap_clusters.png", width = 10, height = 8)
table(cluster = cutree(hc, k = 3), region = meta_qc$region)

## 5e. Visualisation-only correction for technical covariates
# (Never feed these corrected values into DESeq2 — covariates go in the design.)
tech <- model.matrix(~ scale(log(colSums(counts_f))) + ph + pmi + age, data = meta_qc)[, -1]
vmat_corr <- removeBatchEffect(vmat, covariates = tech,
                               design = model.matrix(~ region + diagnosis, meta_qc))
pca_corr <- run_pca(vmat_corr, meta_qc)
ggplot(pca_corr$df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = region, shape = diagnosis)) + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "PCA after regressing out technical covariates (visualisation only)")
ggsave("figures/Q5_pca_corrected.png", width = 7, height = 5)

###############################################################################
# Q6. Is the preprocessed dataset suitable for the next parts?
###############################################################################
# Design balance per region (power) and confounding of covariates with diagnosis
table(meta_qc$region, meta_qc$diagnosis)
for (v in intersect(c("age", "ph", "pmi"), names(meta_qc)))
  print(c(v, signif(kruskal.test(meta_qc[[v]] ~ meta_qc$diagnosis)$p.value, 3)))
chisq.test(table(meta_qc$diagnosis, meta_qc$sex), simulate.p.value = TRUE)

# Save the analysis-ready objects
saveRDS(list(counts = counts_f, meta = meta_qc, dds = dds, vsd = vsd),
        "GSE80655_preprocessed.rds")
sessionInfo()

```
